decisions.issues: Minor: a few small puddles on the laterite rampart floor suggest earlier rain, while the caption says the rain had not yet fallen. They read as old monsoon wet, so this is acceptable. Low dark-bellied clouds, flat husk-fire smoke along the beach and three small grey ships at anchor all match the script. No text in the art. The wide cloud band at the top leaves room for the caption.

Minor: the surf shows some whitecaps rather than truly sluggish waves, but the haze and still palms carry the heavy-air beat. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch13 row: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a gold ear stud. He is in three-quarter back view on the same laterite rampart, with the same domed sentry turret as 1.1. The grey sky on the upper right has room for both captions.

Minor: the boy faces out to sea rather than turning down toward the runner, though the runner at the foot of the tower is clearly looking up at him. The beat reads: one hand shades his eyes and the other arm is flung toward the sea from the top of a lashed palm-trunk tower. Anatomy is sound and there is no text. A large open sky on the right takes both captions.

Minor: the ground at the gate is puddled, which hints at rain, though dripping seawater and earlier monsoon wet can explain it. The cousin has a beard, which the script does not forbid. Ibrahim matches his sheet: white turban, grey-flecked beard, short teal coat over a cream vest with bulging pockets, the scar on his LEFT side from ear to jaw, short and broad, and grinning. He wrings teal coat cloth at his cuff while water drips, and his hands are sound. The cousin is taller and thinner, bare-chested in a checked lungi, with no coat and no scar. The fort gate is the same laterite as 1.1 and 1.2. The sky on the upper right has room for the caption.

v01 is not acceptable. 1) Framing: the script asks for a tight insert of a leaf and a stylus, but v01 is a medium shot of the whole figure with two extra turbaned men in a doorway, and it duplicates the 2.1 setup. 2) Action: the stylus point is pressed into the leaf as if writing, not held still above one name. No list of names shows, only the edge of a closed bundle. 3) Likeness: this Ramayyan has a grey moustache and slicked-back grey hair. The sheet shows him clean-shaven with curly black hair around a receding crown. In this form he would merge with Mathoo Tharakan (grey receding hair, fine grey moustache), which the bible forbids.
decisions.correction: Make this a TIGHT CLOSE-UP INSERT, not a figure shot. The frame is filled by one single unbound palm-leaf strip lying flat and open on a dark wooden low writing desk, seen from slightly above. Across its surface run five or six short horizontal rows of fine, dark, scratched incised strokes, abstract marks only, with no legible letters, no script-like glyphs and no numerals. Ramayyan's thin, brown right hand enters from the top edge, with only the hand, the wrist and the edge of a plain white cotton cloth showing. It holds a slim iron stylus whose point HOVERS a finger's width above one row, clearly lifted and stopped, NOT touching the leaf. No face, no head, no other people, no doorway, no courtyard. Use warm, low light from a small brass oil lamp with an open wick just out of frame, and keep the same dark wood desk and woven mat as the war-hall anteroom. Leave a plain, low-detail band of dark desk surface along the bottom quarter of the frame, clear of the hand and the stylus point, for two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the background banners carry a gold elephant on red rather than the Travancore silver conch (no lettering), and the courtyard stones look damp under overcast haze, with no falling rain visible. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch13 row: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud. Ramayyan matches his sheet and keeps his eyes on the leaf. The red laterite wall above Ramayyan and to the right of Nagoji's head leaves ample space for both balloons in reading order.

Padmini herself is excellent and on-sheet. But a bare-chested man with full long black hair in a low knot and a thick moustache sits at Ramayyan's writing desk with the stylus. He matches neither Ramayyan (receding hair, clean-shaven, plain white cloth) nor Nagoji (rust-red turban, tunic), and he reads as a bare-headed Nagoji double sitting in Ramayyan's place, which breaks continuity with 2.1 and 2.3. The doorway also shows a wet, misty courtyard, although page 1 says the rain has not yet fallen.
decisions.correction: Show Padmini Amma ALONE in the doorway, with no other person anywhere in the frame. Remove the seated man at the low writing desk entirely, and frame her from inside the anteroom so the desk is behind the viewer and out of frame. Keep her exactly as drawn in v01: thick black hair coiled at the nape, gold ball earrings, gold bead necklace, cream sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape hitched for walking, barefoot, leaning on her long walking stick, with a wry half-smile, the sound that is not quite a laugh. Keep the dark wooden door frame and warm laterite wall. Outside the doorway: heavy, low, grey overcast sky, still palms, a DRY stone courtyard and no falling rain, because the rain has not yet fallen. Leave the plain laterite wall to her right clear and low-detail for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Three problems. (1) The framing is a three-quarter figure shot that repeats 2.1, not the script's close-up of 'Nagoji's face' turning from her to Ramayyan. (2) Nagoji's chin and jaw carry visible stippled stubble, but CONTINUITY requires a clean-shaven chin outside captivity. (3) Two background guards wear tan or khaki tunics with shoulder cross-straps and khaki turbans, which read as uniformed sepoys and contradict the chapter's Nair lock (bare-chested, short white mundu, front topknot, no coats or uniforms). Ramayyan and his desk are good.
decisions.correction: Make this a head-and-shoulders CLOSE-UP of Nagoji's face filling the left two-thirds of the frame. His head is turning away from the doorway on the left toward Ramayyan on the right, his eyes sliding right. Keep the v01 rust-red turban, long curly black hair, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud and cream tunic with red sash, but give him a completely CLEAN-SHAVEN chin and jaw, with no stubble, stipple or beard shadow. At the lower right, show Ramayyan bowed over his palm leaf as in v01: receding hairline with curly black hair at the sides, clean-shaven, plain white cloth, his stylus moving on the leaf on the low dark wooden desk, beside a brass oil lamp with an open wick. Draw no soldiers or guards anywhere, in particular no tan or khaki tunics, cross-belts or uniform-like dress. Keep the warm laterite wall and dark wooden pillars, and leave the upper-right wall clear and low-detail for one caption.

decisions.issues: The hand, stick, cord and lac seal work well, with no legible script and an unreadable seal. But a bearded, topknotted, bare-chested man sits at the writing desk in the background with his face visible. He is not Ramayyan, who sits at that desk in 2.1 and 2.3, so the room's continuity breaks. The ola is drawn as a thick wooden board, not a thin palm-leaf strip. The doorway shows bright blue sky with white clouds, while 2.1 and 2.2 are heavily overcast.
decisions.correction: Keep v01's insert composition: Padmini's hand with its gold bangle holding the letter at centre, her other hand on the long walking stick at left against her cream gold-bordered sari, and the cord hanging loose from the end of the leaf with a small red-brown lac seal on the thread. Make the ola a THIN, slightly curved strip of dried palm leaf in pale straw colour, with a small hole near one end for the cord, not a thick wooden board; fine incised lines only, no dark rows of script-like marks. Show NO person in the background: remove the bearded, topknotted man at the desk. Behind the hand put only the laterite wall, dark wooden pillars and a brass oil lamp with an open wick, softly out of focus. Through the doorway: heavy, low, grey overcast sky and still palms as in 2.1 and 2.2, not blue sky with white clouds. Leave the upper-right wall and the top band clear and low-detail for two captions.

decisions.issues: Padmini is on-sheet, and her gaze to the middle distance is right. But a bearded, topknotted, bare-chested man sits at Ramayyan's writing desk and looks up at her, prominent and fully readable. He replaces Ramayyan from 2.1 and 2.3 with a different face. Two turbaned, moustached men stand in the doorway, and their dress matches neither Ramayyan, Nagoji nor the Nair lock (front topknot, short mundu). The leaf in her hand carries dense dark rows of script-like marks, which read as pseudo-text. The leaf is held at chest height rather than lowered.
decisions.correction: Show Padmini Amma ALONE in the anteroom, with no other person in the frame. Remove the bearded man at the writing desk, keep the desk out of frame, and remove the two turbaned men in the doorway. Keep her as drawn in v01: thick black hair coiled at the nape, gold ball earrings, gold bead necklace, cream sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape, the long walking stick in one hand. Her other hand holds the palm-leaf letter LOWERED to waist height, while her eyes look away from it into the middle distance, her face still and thoughtful. The letter is a thin, pale, dried palm-leaf strip with fine incised lines only, no dark rows of script-like marks, its cord hanging loose with a small lac seal. Keep the warm laterite wall, dark wooden pillars and hanging brass oil lamp with open wicks. Through the doorway: heavy, low, grey overcast sky and a dry courtyard as in 2.1, with no rain. Leave the plain laterite wall to her right clear and low-detail for two balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 has a good composition and a correct Padmini: cream sari with a gold border, old drape with no blouse, black hair coiled at the nape, gold stud earrings and necklace, barefoot on the bund, stick in hand, pointing up at pepper vines on living support trees above terraced paddy. There is open sky at upper left for the caption and balloon. It fails on two counts. (1) Anachronism: the two village women working the vines at right, one of them large in the right foreground, wear stitched red short-sleeved blouses. In 1740s Travancore that is a 19th-century garment. A prior review in this project (ch9 4.3 servant) corrected the same fault. (2) Neighbour continuity: the headman here has a full grey-black beard, a gold-striped turban and a staff. In 3.2 (v01, acceptable) the headman has only a moustache, a clean chin, a plain white head-band and empty hands, so the reader sees two different headmen in consecutive panels. Regenerating 3.1 to match 3.2 fixes both.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: Padmini barefoot on the earth bund at left-centre, stick in her right hand, left arm extended pointing up and to the right at the pepper vines climbing the support trees, the terraced paddies and misty hills behind her at left, open grey sky in the upper left kept clear for lettering, and villagers working the vines at right. Change only two things. First, every village woman among the vines wears 1740s Kerala dress: a plain off-white or earth-toned mundu with a single cloth draped over one shoulder or tied above the chest, bare arms and shoulders, and NO stitched blouse, no sleeves and no fitted bodice of any colour. The two women at right must not wear red short-sleeved blouses. Second, the village headman standing beside Padmini must match the next panel: a man of about forty-five with a thick black moustache and a CLEAN-SHAVEN chin and jaw (no beard of any kind), a plain white head cloth tied as a band around his head, a white gold-striped towel hanging over both shoulders, a bare chest, a cream mundu with a narrow gold-striped border, and empty hands with no staff.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Padmini matches her sheet and bible line: cream sari with a gold border, old drape with no blouse, black hair coiled at the nape, gold earrings and necklace, stick, barefoot. She is already walking on past the grinning headman, whose hands are pressed together, which reads well as being caught out. The pepper vines are on living support trees, with terraced paddy behind. There is no text and the hands are sound. Minor points: two small background women (upper left and lower right) appear to wear short-sleeved blouses. They are tiny, matching the earlier precedent of tolerated background blouses. This headman (moustache only, white head-band) differs from the bearded headman in 3.1 v01, so 3.1 is being regenerated to match this one. Lettering: Padmini's balloon goes in the open sky to the right of her head (upper centre-right). The headman's short balloon goes at the top between his head and hers, overlapping the foliage at top left if needed.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches the commander sheet and the ch13 row: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, a clean chin with only faint shading, a tiny flush gold ear stud, cream tunic with sleeves down to the wrists, broad red sash, brass-hilted sword as on his sheet, and boots. Padmini matches her sheet. The setting is a laterite rampart under midday overcast light, with Dutch ships at anchor offshore. Men below along the wall haul cannon on ropes beside stacked shot. Flags are plain red with no marks. There is no text and the anatomy is sound. Deviations: Nagoji walks nearly level beside her rather than a full pace behind. The tip of her stick runs out of the bottom of the frame instead of being shown on the stone. Her right hand hangs close to Nagoji's scabbard tip, a slight tangent that still reads as depth. Lettering: the large open sky at upper right easily takes both small Padmini balloons. The 3.4 inset should go in the lower-right corner, over the wall and shot, not the lower left, where Nagoji's boots are.

Acceptable for a small hands-only inset. Padmini's cream sari with its gold border, her gold bangle and her stick hand identify her. Her other hand rests on folded bolts of cloth while soldiers' wives take cloth and a measure of rice from the baskets in a laterite storeroom, with the fort visible through the doorway. That is the afternoon beat. Every hand is sound: four hands on the measure and the cloth, each traced to a wrist and arm. The flag in the doorway carries only a dark emblem, with no lettering. Minor: the cropped wife at upper right shows a short rust-red sleeve under her green drape, likely a stitched blouse. It is small and cropped at inset size, so it is noted but tolerated. Padmini's face is out of frame, so her balloon tail points to the top edge above her neckline (upper left). Lettering: the plain laterite wall at top centre, between the cloth stacks and the doorway.

v01 gets almost everything right. It has a sunset estate yard with the great jackfruit tree over a stone platform, horse lines along the compound wall, jar carriers walking off, women lighting brass lamps along the verandah in the old drape, and the Nair house with its tiered tile roofs. Padmini (correct) and Nagoji face each other. Nagoji's face is correct: moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, rust turban, red sash, sword and boots. Failure: his LEFT sleeve is pushed up to the elbow, and his bare left forearm shows a large mottled pale scar patch on the outer, back-of-hand side. The prompt requires that in present scenes his sleeves stay down to the wrists. Even when the brand is shown, the bible puts it on the INNER forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, as a defined patch beside a thin white scar. This mark is on the wrong face of the arm and runs most of its length. It is also inconsistent with 3.3, where both sleeves are down. Minor, not the reason for rejection: the jar carriers read as grown men rather than boys, and the space for Nagoji's balloon beside his turban is tight.
decisions.correction: Keep this image exactly as it is: sunset light, the great jackfruit tree over the worn stone platform, the horse lines along the compound wall at left, the jar carriers, the women lighting lamps on the verandah, Padmini at left with her stick gesturing toward Nagoji, and Nagoji at right facing her with rust-red turban, tiny gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, red sash, sword and boots. Change one thing only. Nagoji's LEFT sleeve (the arm on the viewer's right, whose hand holds the scabbard) must come down to the wrist like his right sleeve: a full cream tunic sleeve covering the whole forearm to the wrist, with only the back of his hand showing below the cuff. No forearm skin, brand, scar, burn patch or mark may be visible on either arm.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Padmini in close-up matches her sheet: thick black hair coiled at the nape (the faint silvery lines read as sheen, not grey), gold stud earring and bead necklace, cream sari with a gold border in the old drape with no blouse, gold bangle, hand on her stick. Her face is lit warm orange by the last light. She looks right, past the frame, toward the sea and the setting sun. The setting is the same as 3.5 (Nair house with brass lamps, jackfruit tree over the stone platform, horse lines at the compound wall). There is no text and the hand is sound. Minor: one horse in the line at far right is white or grey, while the horse line in 3.5 is all dark, and the bible keeps greys out of the Madurai troop. It is small and at the frame edge. Lettering: the open orange sky at upper right, between the jackfruit foliage and the sun, takes both Padmini balloons, with tails running left to her mouth.

v01 is otherwise strong: overcast light, hooves in the wash, a long file, Nagoji at the head on the right matching his sheet (curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, rust turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots), Kayal correct (ochre bay, black mane and lower legs, no white), Maravar riders bare-headed in short brown jackets and hitched mundus, and open sky for the three captions. It fails on one figure. The second-rank Madurai rider at about x 0.23 wears a deep GREEN turban. The bible says Raza Khan alone wears green, so readers will take him for Raza. But he has a full bushy black beard, a fuller face and a gold ear stud, not Raza's lean hawk face with a grey-streaked goatee and pointed moustache. Panel 4.5 on the same page draws Raza correctly, so the page would show two different Razas. If he is meant as an ordinary trooper instead, the bible bans green turbans in the Madurai troop. His head is about 11% of frame height, too big to ignore.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition and nothing else changes: the wide overcast beach, horses walking in the shallow wash along the tide line, the long loose file receding to the left, and Nagoji at the head on the right in his rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers and boots, riding Kayal (ochre red-brown bay, black mane, tail and lower legs, no white markings). Change only the Madurai riders: EVERY Madurai rider wears a high-wrapped WHITE or off-white turban with a knee-length white jama and a plain cloth waistband. There is NO green turban anywhere in this panel (Raza Khan is not shown here). No rider except Nagoji wears an ear stud. The Maravar riders stay bare-headed with short curly hair, short dark jackets and hitched white mundus, on visibly smaller ponies whose backs are about a head lower than the tall dark Madurai horses. Keep the top third as open, low-detail overcast sky, clear of palm fronds and lance tips, for three caption boxes.

decisions.issues: Minor. The small, soft background riders on the far left wear dark turbans and red cross-sashes, and one wears a rust-red turban. That does not match 4.1's white-turbaned Madurai file and bare-headed Maravar riders, and the bible bans red or rust Madurai turbans. Their heads are only about 3% of frame height, so they cannot be identified at print size. Ponnan wears dark shoes in the stirrup where his sheet is barefoot, and his jacket is plain brown where 4.3 has black with gold trim. The principals are correct: Nagoji (clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, rust turban, red sash) is in the left foreground on Kayal (ochre bay, no white), and Ponnan is half a length back on the right on a smaller dark-bay pony (bare-headed, curly hair, heavy jaw, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, white mundu). There is a large open sky band for all three balloons.

Minor. Ponnan's pony has a small white star on the forehead and is a lighter chestnut-bay than the dark-bay pony in 4.2. With no other horse in frame, it does not read as especially small. His jacket is black with gold trim, matching his sheet's trim but differing from 4.2's plain brown. Ponnan matches his sheet: bare-headed, short curly hair, heavy jaw, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, white mundu, bare feet in the stirrups. He is alone on the beach, gaze off toward the sea. The open overcast sky on the right takes his balloon easily.

v01 gets the beat right: Nagoji on Kayal (correct, no white markings) turned with his right arm out in an open-handed address, white-turbaned Madurai lancers on the left, Maravar riders on the right, and open sky upper right. Two continuity failures. (1) The front Madurai rider at the top-left edge wears a GREEN turban and is again drawn with a full black beard and a gold ear stud. By the bible's green-turban rule he reads as Raza Khan, but his face does not match Raza's sheet or the correct Raza in 4.5. (2) The Maravar riders are bare-chested with only white shoulder cloths. The page notes, 4.1 and Ponnan in 4.2 and 4.3 all give them short dark jackets, so the same men change costume within the page.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: Nagoji at centre on Kayal (ochre red-brown bay, black mane and lower legs, no white markings) in his rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash and boots, torso turned toward the riders, right arm extended with an open hand as he addresses them. The Madurai lancers are on the left, the Maravar riders on the right, and the overcast beach and sea stay as drawn. Fix two things. (1) EVERY Madurai rider wears a high-wrapped WHITE or off-white turban and a white jama. There is NO green turban anywhere in this panel (Raza Khan is not in it), and no rider except Nagoji wears an ear stud. (2) The Maravar riders match panel 4.1: bare-headed with short curly hair, each in a short dark short-sleeved jacket over the chest (not bare-chested), white mundus hitched to the knee, bare legs. They ride smaller ponies whose backs are about a head lower than the Madurai horses. Keep the upper-right sky open and low-detail for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Raza Khan himself is excellent and matches his sheet: deep green high-wrapped turban, lean hawk face, pointed moustache, grey-streaked goatee, and the scar on his anatomical LEFT cheek turned toward camera, with his right hand adjusting the turban. The panel fails on three points. (1) Nagoji's mount, Kayal, has a clear white star or blaze on her forehead. The script and bible say she has no white markings. (2) The background riders wear green turbans and green sashes. Raza alone wears green, and the Madurai troop is white-turbaned, as in 4.1 and 4.4. (3) Framing: Nagoji fills the left 40% as a co-lead instead of sitting at the edge of frame with Raza as the subject.
decisions.correction: Keep Raza Khan exactly as drawn on his black Madurai horse, along with the beach, the surf and the overcast sky: deep green high-wrapped turban, lean face, hawk nose, pointed moustache, grey-streaked goatee, the puckered scar on his anatomical LEFT cheek (our right) turned toward camera in three-quarter view, right hand raised adjusting the turban. Fix three things. (1) Nagoji's mare Kayal has a plain ochre red-brown bay face with NO white star, blaze, stripe or snip anywhere, plus a black mane and black lower legs, exactly as on her sheet. (2) Move Nagoji to the far LEFT EDGE of the frame, his body and horse cropped by the panel border but his face (curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, rust-red turban) still inside the frame and turned toward Raza, so Raza is the clear subject filling the centre and right. (3) Any background riders are Madurai lancers in WHITE or off-white high-wrapped turbans and white jamas, with NO green turbans and no green sashes, since Raza alone wears green. Keep open, low-detail sky above both men's heads for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only: topknots sit on the crown rather than at the front, and one torch burns in daylight. Otherwise it shows the beat: bare-chested Nairs in white mundus cleaning muskets, powder flask, talisman tied on an upper arm, one muttering over his hands, one laughing with head thrown back, shields and swords stacked. Plain unlettered flags. The cloudy sky across the top leaves room for the caption.

Nagoji matches the sheet: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, sleeves to the wrists, red sash, boots, talwar. He crouches among young bare-chested Nairs who have muskets across their knees, and his hands are sound. Minor: three tiny out-of-focus figures in the gateway (around x 0.82, y 0.33) wear brimmed European-looking hats. They are barely legible at print size. The cloudy sky top-left and top-centre is clear for the balloon.

Clean. The young bare-chested Nair with a topknot laughs nervously, hand behind his head and musket held upright. The courtyard and gatehouse match 5.1 and 5.2, and the hands are sound. Minor: the topknot sits on the crown, and the muskets read as flintlocks across the page. The open sky above and left of him has room for both balloons.

Nagoji's face matches the sheet (turban, curled moustache, clean chin, ear stud), and the older Nair with the upright musket fits the beat. But Nagoji's LEFT sleeve is rolled to the elbow, and a pale scar and a puckered patch show on the top/outer side of his palm-down forearm, with the patch near the elbow. This breaks the bible (the brand belongs on the INNER forearm, a hand's width above the wrist). It is also inconsistent with 5.2 and 5.5, where both sleeves are down to the wrists, and the script does not call for the brand here. Minor: a background Nair wears a white head cloth.
decisions.correction: Both of Nagoji's tunic sleeves stay down to the wrists, exactly as in the neighbouring panels: no rolled or pushed-back sleeve, no bare forearm, and no brand, burn, scar or mark visible on either arm or hand. His left hand rests on his knee with the cream sleeve covering the forearm to the wrist. Keep everything else that worked: the same laterite fort courtyard with the tiled gatehouse under cloudy daylight. Nagoji sits on the ground on the left in his rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar, with his thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and small gold ear stud. His head turns toward the older-faced Nair on the right, who is not laughing: bare-chested, front topknot, white mundu, matchlock held upright between his knees. Leave open cloudy sky above both men's heads for two balloons. Background Nair soldiers are bare-chested with front topknots, with no head cloths or turbans.

decisions.issues: Nagoji himself is on model (turban, curled moustache, clean chin, ear stud, sleeves to the wrists, sash, talwar). The panel misses the script framing, though. It is a waist-up medium shot, not close on his face, and the courtyard is sharp, not out of focus. The background soldiers also break the page's Nair look: many wear white headbands or turbans, toga-like white shoulder cloths or tunics, and beards. That is inconsistent with the bare-chested, bare-headed Nairs of 5.1 to 5.4.
decisions.correction: Frame this as a true close-up. Nagoji's head and the top of his shoulders fill most of the frame, his face large in the upper-middle and set slightly to one side. Keep clear, low-detail cloudy sky on the other side and above his turban for three stacked balloons. The courtyard behind him is soft and blurred: only vague shapes of laterite wall, tiled gatehouse roof and seated men, with no sharp detail. Any Nair soldiers visible behind him match the rest of the page: bare-chested, white mundu tied short, hair in a front topknot, no head cloths, headbands, turbans, shoulder cloths, tunics or beards. Keep what worked: rust-red turban, long curly black hair, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, red sash, the same cloudy daylight as the previous panels, and his hard, level gaze.

decisions.issues: Minor only: brass lamps are already lit in daylight, though 8.1 says lamps 'have been lit' later. Nagoji's scabbard reads a little straight for a talwar. All four principals match their sheets. Nagoji has the rust-red turban, a clean chin, the curled moustache and the gold stud. Varma has black hair with a knot on his left side and is bare-chested in cream and gold. Tharakan has grey hair, a grey moustache and the gold cross. Ramayyan sits cross-legged with his bundle and stylus. The map is lines only and there is no text. The open sky band above the table has room for the caption and Varma's balloon. Use this frame as the anchor for Varma's look on the rest of the page.

Varma is drawn with heavily grey-streaked hair and an older, heavier face. That does not match the V13 sheet or panel 6.1, where his hair is black, and it makes him read like a twin of the grey-haired Tharakan. No side knot is visible. He looks down at the map instead of glancing at Tharakan. An unscripted bearded man sits cross-legged at the left edge, where readers may take him for Ramayyan or a new character. The light changes to a sunset glow, unlike the overcast daylight of 6.1. A lamp and a bowl fill the lower right, where the 6.3 inset will sit.
decisions.correction: Marthanda Varma must match panel 6.1 and his V13 sheet: a man in his mid-thirties with JET-BLACK hair and no grey at all, the lean V13 face with strong cheekbones and a thick black curled moustache, bare-headed with his hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, bare-chested, a cream mundu with a gold border and gold necklaces. Mathoo Tharakan (grey receding hair, fine grey moustache, gold cross on his chest, white cloth with a gold border, standing) is the ONLY grey-haired man. Varma's index finger traces the inked coastline at the centre-left of the cloth map while his eyes turn up and sideways in a glance at Tharakan. Only these two at the table: no seated bearded man and no other figure at the frame edges, and any guards must be small and distant. Keep the lower-right quarter of the frame to plain table and map edge, with no lamp or bowl there, because a tight inset will be laid over it. Keep the open sky at upper right clear for two balloons. Use the same open tiled-roof war hall, overcast daylight (no sunset glow) and lines-only cloth map as panel 6.1.

decisions.issues: The script calls for a tight inset of fingers and coin. This is a medium figure shot of Ramayyan with a wide sea view, so it would not work as a small inset. The hands are wrong: two hands hold the bundle and stylus while a third places the coin. The palm-leaf bundle looks like a bundle of straw sticks. Ramayyan has slicked-back straight hair and a bare shoulder, unlike his curly side hair and full white wrap in 6.1 and 6.4. Varma's tracing finger is missing. A bowl of loose coins competes with the single Dutch coin.
decisions.correction: Make this a TIGHT close-up inset, not a figure shot: frame only the cloth map surface at hand height, with no faces, no bodies above the wrists and no sea or hall view. Ramayyan's thin brown fingers, with a fold of plain white cloth at the wrist, set ONE small plain copper coin (its face too small to read) on a mark on the inked coastline. Varma's bare brown index fingertip rests on the same coastline just beside it, entering from the opposite edge of the frame. Show exactly two hands, one each, each with five fingers. No bowl of coins and no other coins. The map is hand-drawn ink on cloth: coastline, rivers and hill marks as lines only, no lettering, with a pebble and a shell token nearby. Keep one corner of plain, low-detail cloth free for a caption.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the cloth map on the table is turned, with the sea on its right side where 6.1 has it on the left. A brass lamp is lit in daylight. Otherwise clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet and 6.1: receding hairline, curly black side hair, white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus. He sits cross-legged, looking up with a faint satisfied smile. The hands are sound, there is no text, and the hall and sky are the same as 6.1. The large open sky in the centre and right has room for the caption and both Ramayyan balloons.

Varma again has grey-streaked hair and an older face, which does not match the V13 sheet or the black-haired Varma of 6.1. He also wears a round gold ear stud, which is Nagoji's identifier. The script asks for two profiles; this shows two three-quarter views. The same unscripted bearded man as in 6.2 sits at the left edge, this time with a sword, adding a third figure to a two-person panel.
decisions.correction: Marthanda Varma must match panel 6.1 and his V13 sheet: mid-thirties, JET-BLACK hair with no grey streaks, the lean V13 face with strong cheekbones and a thick black curled moustache, his hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, NO gold ear stud, bare-chested, a cream mundu with a gold border and gold necklaces. Mathoo Tharakan is the only grey-haired man: grey receding hair, fine grey moustache, gold cross on his chest, white cloth with a gold border. Draw them as two true side profiles facing each other across the cloth map, Tharakan on the left and Varma on the right, both bent slightly over the map, which is lines only with no lettering. No third person: no seated bearded man at the left edge and no figures at the table. Use the same open tiled-roof war hall and overcast daylight as panel 6.1. Keep the open sky in the upper middle, between and above their heads, clear for Tharakan's long balloon and Varma's reply.

decisions.issues: The direction of travel is reversed. Every ox pair and merchant faces left and walks downhill: the lead cart is lowest in the foreground and the line trails up the hill to the right. The convoy is heading toward the sea in the far left distance, when the beat is carts CLIMBING a ghat pass inland with the empty sea behind them, carrying pepper away from the blockaded harbours. Everything else works: forested ghat, pepper sacks, paired bullocks, Syrian Christian merchants in white walking beside the wheels, an empty sea with no ships, no text, and wide sky for the voice-over box.
decisions.correction: Reverse the direction of travel so the convoy visibly climbs AWAY from the sea. The red earth road rises from the lower-left foreground to the upper right, deeper into the forested hills. Every pair of yoked humped bullocks, every cart and every merchant faces and walks toward the upper right, uphill. The lead cart is highest on the road and the line trails back down toward the viewer. The empty sea, with no ships, lies behind them in the far left distance. Keep everything else: the misty forested ghat, heavy wooden carts piled with tied pepper sacks, Syrian Christian merchants in white mundus, shoulder cloths and white head cloths walking beside the wheels, the full-width strip format and the wide overcast sky across the top for the voice-over box.

decisions.issues: Most of v01 works: the burning town, smoke columns, distant ships with small gun flashes, the refugee column on the palm road and an open grey sky for both captions. But at least four or five VOC soldiers in blue coats, tricornes and white cross-belts walk in the middle of the refugee column next to the bullock carts. That contradicts the beat: in November the Dutch only bombarded from the sea ('Three days, and then they sailed away'), and 7.2 is where they first land ('In February, they came back to stay'). There is also a faint scribble like a signature over the fence in the bottom-right corner.
decisions.correction: Keep the composition, the muted grey flashback palette, the burning roofs and smoke columns, the distant ships with small gun flashes and the open grey sky across the upper part. But there are NO European or blue-coated soldiers anywhere on land. In November the Dutch only bombarded from the sea and never came ashore, so no tricornes, blue coats, white cross-belts or European muskets appear among the people on the palm road, on the beach or in the town. The column streaming inland is only Colachel townsfolk (fisher families, women with bundles and baskets on their heads, children, a few bullock carts), with at most a few bare-chested Travancore Nair soldiers in white mundus tied short, with front topknots and matchlocks. The Dutch appear only as the distant ships offshore. No signature, monogram or scribble in any corner.

decisions.issues: Clean. Longboats are beaching at dawn under cannon smoke from the ships; VOC soldiers in blue coats and tricornes wade ashore; the Nair soldiers are bare-chested, in white mundus tied short, with front topknots and long guns, falling back into the dunes and palms. No text, blood or bad anatomy. The upper-left sky is clear for both captions. The palette is a little warmer than 7.1 and 7.3 but still muted.

v01 has the distant view, the smoke, the burned houses and a longboat rowing toward an anchored ship, but it fails on several points. (1) A long intact stone fortress wall with bastions runs along the beach, and a European castle or lighthouse-like tower stands on the headland. Neither is in the script, and an intact stone fort clashes with the half-built mud fort in 7.4. (2) The 'temple' is a tall gopuram fused onto a European gabled building, and its tiled roof looks intact, not scorched. (3) The figures in the longboat read as hooded adults or monks, not as captive women and children, so the slave-sale beat behind Ramayyan's lines is lost. (4) The rendering is soft and photographic, not the clean ink line of the neighbouring panels.
decisions.correction: Keep the distant view from the rocky shore, the grey smoke drifting over the water, the burned palm-thatch houses, and the anchored ship with a single longboat pulling toward it, oars rising. Draw it in the same clean ink line and painted colour as the neighbouring panels, not a soft photographic painting. Tengapattanam is an undefended fishing village: no stone walls, bastions, fortress, castle, church tower or lighthouse anywhere on the shore or headland. The temple is a low Kerala temple with a sloping tiled roof that is visibly scorched and blackened, with smoke rising from it; never a European gabled building and never a tall tower. In the longboat, the small huddled shapes must clearly read as captive women in saris with their heads covered and small children pressed against them, with two or three rowers at the oars; no hoods, and no soldiers seated as passengers. Keep the open grey sky in the upper part clear for two lettering lines.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Karl August matches his sheet: cropped grey hair, grey moustache and stubble, a gaunt sallow face, a stained rough cotton shirt. He sits in a soft-edged vignette inset in the lower-left corner. The half-built fort has scaffolding and a mud bastion slumping under a cannon, with earth sliding off. There are rotting sacks and puddles, and sick blue-coated soldiers lie under a thin awning. The flag is plain horizontal red, white and blue bands with no monogram, and there is no text. The upper-right sky is clear for the caption and Karl's memory box. Minor: the distant departing ships slightly anticipate 7.5, and Karl's yellow cast is mild (sallow rather than jaundiced).

Clean. This is a full-width strip: ships under full sail standing out to sea with plain tricolour flags and no lettering, and a thin line of blue-coated VOC soldiers on the beach watching them go beside the unfinished mud wall, cannon and awning. It matches 7.4's fort, so the page stays consistent. A wide open sky across the top holds both Karl memory boxes. The palette is somewhat bluer and brighter than a strict desaturated flashback, but in line with 7.4. Karl is off-panel and his lines are tailless memory boxes, so the tail points are nominal (lower-left edge, toward where his inset sat in 7.4).

Acceptable with minor faults. The cast is correct: Nagoji on the left in the commander look (rust-red turban, red sash, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, small gold stud), Ramayyan seated in the centre with a palm-leaf bundle and stylus (receding hair, clean-shaven, plain white), and Varma on the right (bare-headed, bare-chested, gold necklaces, cream mundu with gold border) with a hand on the map. The night war hall with small brass open-wick lamps is right, the map has ink lines only with no text, and there is clear night sky and roof for both balloons, Ramayyan's first and Varma's second. Minor faults: (1) Nagoji has light stippled stubble on his chin and jaw. At print size it reads as shading, but the bible asks for a clean chin. (2) Varma has a whitish-grey streak at his temple, and his hair is in a crown knot, not a side knot above the LEFT ear (the same crown knot as page 6). (3) Nagoji's sleeves are pushed up, and the brand shows as a pale blurred patch on his crossed LEFT forearm. The ch13 row allows this. (4) Nagoji stands at the end of the table, not exactly across it.

Acceptable. The beat reads clearly: Nagoji leans in with his left hand flat on the map, and Varma cuts across him with a calm raised palm. Nagoji's chin is essentially clean, with a thick curled moustache, a gold stud and the commander dress. Varma's face matches his sheet, with black hair, gold beads and a cream and gold mundu. The map has no lettering, the hands are sound and the lamps have open wicks. Nagoji's balloon fits top-left over the roof and pillar, and Varma's two fit in the upper-right sky or the sky between their heads. Faults: (1) An unscripted seated courtier sits large in the right foreground: bearded, grey-flecked hair in a bun, rudraksha beads, hand at his chin. He appears in no other usable panel on the page and could be misread as an off-model Ramayyan. (2) A bare-chested spear guard stands in the background right. (3) Varma's hair is in a crown knot, not a LEFT side knot. (4) Nagoji's sleeve is pushed up, showing the pale brand patch and the thin white scar on his LEFT forearm, which the ch13 row allows. (5) The copper coin sits in the blue sea wash just off the coastline.

Rejected. The framing is wrong: the script asks for an overhead view on the cloth map, but v01 is an eye-level medium shot of Varma bending over the table. Readable unscripted men fill the panel. A bare-chested bearded man with a red waist sash and hand on chin stands upper left, a bearded seated courtier sits at the right, and two spear guards stand behind. Nagoji and Ramayyan both speak in this panel from off-frame, so readers would take these off-model men for them. The sea side of the map is at the lower left, so the 8.4 inset in the upper corner cannot sit over it. The coin sits in the water, not on the coast mark.
decisions.correction: Reframe as a true top-down overhead shot looking straight down onto the hand-drawn cloth map, with the map filling most of the frame and the dark wooden table edge showing only at the borders. Draw no heads, faces or bodies of any person anywhere in the panel: no standing or seated men, no bearded onlookers, no guards. The only figure is Varma's right hand and bare forearm with a gold bangle, entering from the lower-right edge. His fingertips sweep a short line of five or six dark river pebbles inland across the dashed inland-road line just behind the coast mark, closing the road. Turn the map so the sea side (pale blue-grey wash) runs along the top of the frame, filling the upper-left corner where the inset will sit. The coastline crosses the upper third, and the single small copper coin, its face too small to read, sits exactly on the coastline, not in the water. Keep the map as ink lines only (coast, rivers, small hill marks, the dashed road) with scattered pebble and shell tokens, no lettering, place names, grid or compass rose. Keep warm light from small brass open-wick lamps at the table edge. Leave the plain inland cloth in the lower-left and lower-centre of the map low-detail for three balloons.

decisions.issues: Acceptable, with no significant faults. Mukkuvar fishermen kneel and paddle low kattumaram rafts of four or five rough logs lashed with rope, with no sails and no lights. They slip between dark, unlit hulls of period three-masted ships at night. There is no text, and the anatomy and paddle grips are sound. No face can be read: all the fishermen are seen from behind. Both lines are voice-overs, lettered as tailless boxes, so no tail points are given. The clear starry sky at top centre (about x 0.35-0.62, y 0-0.18) and the dark open water at lower right (about x 0.6-1.0, y 0.65-1.0) hold the two boxes. The panel will be scaled down as an inset in the upper corner of 8.3.

Rejected. The man Varma addresses, in the right foreground (over the shoulder, presumably Nagoji), is off-model: bearded, no rust-red turban, a large hanging gold earring, and a maroon cloth over white. Varma himself has grey-streaked hair worn loose, not black hair in a knot, which reads as the older figure from his sheet. The panel is crowded with unscripted readable men: a standing bearded man with arms crossed, a bald man with forehead marks who could be mistaken for Ramayyan, a seated grey-bearded courtier, and two bearded guards. The beat (Varma turned full on Nagoji, direct and level) gets lost, and the page's cast becomes confused.
decisions.correction: Draw Varma alone, seen from Nagoji's point of view across the table. Varma stands upright behind the cloth map, turned square to the viewer, framed from the waist up. His level, direct gaze looks straight out of the panel. One hand rests flat on the map; the other hangs at his side, not pointing. Match his V13 sheet face: thick moustache, clean chin, pearl ear drops. His hair is fully black with no grey at all, tied in a knot (side knot above his LEFT ear). He is bare-headed and bare-chested, with gold bead necklaces and a cream mundu with a gold border. Draw no other person: no over-the-shoulder foreground figure, no Nagoji, no seated or standing courtiers, no bald man with forehead marks, no guards or bystanders. Keep the night war hall: timber pillars, a sloping tiled roof, the open side onto the dark moonlit sea with palms, and small brass open-wick lamps on the table. The map edge shows ink lines only, with no lettering. Leave the dark night sky and roof band on both sides of his head clear for three balloons.

decisions.issues: Rejected. The two principals and the coin between them are right: Nagoji points at the coin and Varma leans on the table. But a sharply drawn seated man in white cloth sits at the centre back of the table, the spot Ramayyan holds in 8.1. He has a thick moustache and full black hair, so he reads as an off-model Ramayyan in the middle of the strip. Four background guards wear rust-red turbans, white tunics and red sashes, so they read as copies of Nagoji's commander dress, while the other panels' guards are bare-chested Nairs. Ships with lit windows sit at a quay by a fort just outside the hall, unlike the open dark sea in 8.1 to 8.5. Nagoji also shows light stubble on his chin and jaw.
decisions.correction: Keep the wide bottom-strip composition. Nagoji stands on the left: rust-red turban, cream tunic with the sleeves down, broad red sash, talwar, leaning over the table with one finger near the copper coin. Varma stands on the right: bare-headed, bare-chested, gold bead necklaces, cream mundu with a gold border, both hands on the table. The two face each other in profile across the cloth map, with the small copper coin on the coastline between them. Remove the seated man at the centre back of the table and every other person: no seated courtier, no guards. In particular, draw no background men in red turbans or red sashes. Behind the two men, show only the hall's timber pillars, the laterite half-wall, the dark open sea and palms under a night sky. Draw no ships, harbour, quay, fort walls or lit windows. Nagoji's chin and jaw are clean-shaven and smooth with no stubble, and he wears a tiny flush gold ear stud. Varma's hair is fully black. Keep the map as ink lines only with no lettering, and keep the small brass open-wick lamps. Leave the roof band at the top-left corner and the night-sky band between and above their heads low-detail for a caption and two balloons.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Laterite wall, low tiled roofs, long rows of open-wick lamps, worshippers cupping the flames and one man pressing his palms to his eyes, thin rain at night. The upper centre-right sky is clear for the caption, and there is no painted text. Minor points for the author: the foreground woman (and two in the background) wear short-sleeved stitched blouses. The bible bans stitched blouses only for Padmini, but they are doubtful for 1740s Kerala. There is also one tiny background figure at the right edge (about x 0.83, y 0.68) in a dark coat and trousers.

Acceptable. Padmini matches her sheet: cream sari with gold border in the old drape, no blouse, gold necklace and earrings, walking stick, hair coiled at the nape. She hands a red packet to a bare-chested Nair soldier in a short white mundu. A second soldier has a white packet tied at his wrist. The Madurai riders (white high turbans, white jamas, dark horses, plain lances) hang back at the edge of the light. Minor: her tray of packets rests against her waist with no hand under it. The Nair topknots sit on the crown rather than at the front. The soldiers carry spears and swords, not matchlocks. There is a small dot on Padmini's forehead that is not on her sheet. The panel has no lettering.

Acceptable. Ibrahim matches his sheet: white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat, vest with pockets, striped shawl, sandals. He crouches and sets a brass lamp on the lowest step among the others. Nagoji crouches beside him and matches the bible: thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots and talwar. Only the outer side of his left forearm shows, so the brand stays hidden. Ibrahim's scarred left cheek is turned away. Minor: his other hand also touches a second brass lamp. The top-centre sky (x 0.35 to 0.6, y 0 to 0.25) is clear for both balloons.

Acceptable. Raza Khan matches his sheet: green high-wrapped turban, hawk nose, pointed moustache, goatee, scar on the anatomical left cheek, green drape. He raises his palms in prayer, looking toward the sea, with his Madurai men in white turbans and jamas standing apart with dark horses. Minor: two lances stand upright on the paving with no one holding them. Raza's lips are closed, not visibly moving. The top-left and top-centre sky is clear for the caption.

Acceptable. Nagoji and Ibrahim are seen from behind, looking out over the temple wall at the dark sea, with the tiny lights of three distant ships. Costumes match panel 3. Nagoji's ear stud and moustache tip show in lost profile. Minor: Ibrahim has a small gold ear stud that is not on his sheet, and he turns toward Nagoji rather than out to sea. The large open sky in the upper half holds all three balloons easily.

Minor: the father's fingertips rest on the child's forehead and hair rather than clearly tracing the face. Everything else in the beat is there: the wide estate at night, the woman at the rice jar, folded white cloth on the shelf behind her, and the jackfruit tree and horse lines that match 10.2 to 10.5. The lamps have open wicks, there is no painted text, and the night sky in the upper centre is clear for the caption.

Minor: Dhanaji's right hand holds the whetstone tight against the guard instead of mid-blade, but it still reads as sharpening. Both men match their sheets. Dhanaji sits on a low stool on the left in a white pagdi and indigo quilted tunic, with a short beard and no sash. Nagoji sits on the tree platform on the right in the rust-red turban and red sash, with a clean-shaven chin, the gold ear stud and the talwar across his knees. A brass open-wick lamp sits on the ground between them. The caption fits in the upper-left sky and the Dhanaji balloon fits above the roofline at top centre.

Minor: he grips a short sheathed sword held upright rather than the bare talwar across his knees from 10.2, and the lamplight from below is soft rather than strong. Nagoji is on-model: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with only slight shading, small gold ear stud and the rust-red turban, with a clear corner-of-the-mouth smile. The dark sky at upper right takes both balloons without touching his face.

Minor: Dhanaji sits on the edge of the stone tree platform instead of the low stool from 10.2. A small brass hanging lamp in the background could read as glass-globed, but it is tiny and off the main action. He matches his sheet (short black beard, white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, no sash), the whetstone is pressed on the blade, his expression is serious, and his hands are sound. Nagoji is off-panel to the right, where he sits in 10.2. Both balloons fit in the night sky between the tree and the roof, top centre to top right.

The only candidate (v01) breaks continuity with the panels on either side and misplays Dhanaji's beat. Both men are crouched on their heels on bare ground and Dhanaji's stool has gone. His talwar is sheathed at his hip, although 10.4 shows him sharpening it and 11.1 has the blade across his knees. He gazes up into the tree canopy above and past Nagoji, so his surprise reads as a reaction to something overhead, not to Nagoji's words. The two men are also fairly large for a 'small under the tree' wide shot. The identities are correct (Nagoji has a clean chin and the ear stud, Dhanaji the white pagdi and indigo tunic). The setting is right: the brass open-wick lamp between them, horse lines with heads low, and sleeping riders on mats.
decisions.correction: Keep this wide night composition: the jackfruit tree with its low stone platform, the tiled estate house behind, the horse lines with heads hanging low and the riders asleep on woven mats on the right, the small brass oil lamp with an open wick and no glass chimney on the ground between the two men, and both men's costumes exactly as drawn. Fix posture and eyelines to match the panels before and after. Neither man squats or crouches. Dhanaji (short black beard, white Maratha pagdi turban, indigo quilted tunic, no sash) sits on the left on the same low wooden stool as in the earlier panel. His bare talwar lies across his knees with the whetstone still in one hand. He has just lifted his head from the blade and turned it toward Nagoji, eyebrows raised, mouth slightly open, eyes on Nagoji's face and not on the sky or the tree. Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, boots, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud) sits on a low stone ledge on the right with his talwar across his knees, head bowed, gazing at the lamp flame and not at Dhanaji. Make both men small in the frame, each about a third of the frame height, and leave the dark sky in the upper right open and empty. The sleeping riders lie on their sides under blankets with their heads on rolled cloth, clearly asleep and not face-down.

decisions.issues: Minor: Dhanaji's look reads more wary than softened, with a furrowed brow as he glances up to the left. He sits on a stone ledge rather than 10.2's low stool, but he squats in 10.5 too, so the page is already inconsistent there. Otherwise he matches the sheet: white pagdi, short black beard, indigo quilted tunic, no sash, gold hoop. The blade lies across his lap, and the brass lamp has an open wick on the ground. Hands are sound and there is no text. The night sky at upper right is clear for both balloons.

Minor: this is a medium shot of the seated Nagoji with his chin on his fist, not a tight face shot, and Keshavrao reaches upward as he goes under rather than plainly sinking. The beat still reads. The storm-water memory bleeds in from the left. A rope runs through bandaged palms and its frayed end whips loose, tied to no one. Keshavrao has hacked short hair, a faint moustache, rags and paired ankle chains, and no rope comes near his neck or body. Nagoji is on-model: thick moustache, clean chin, gold stud, rust-red turban, red sash, boots, sleeves down. The caption can sit on the low-detail ground at lower left or in the top-centre sky. Nagoji's balloon fits over the dim house and sky left of his head.

Clean. Dhanaji is on the left, whetstone on the blade, on-model. Nagoji is on the right with his hand on the talwar hilt and the blade across his knees. He has a clean chin, thick moustache, gold stud, rust-red turban, sleeves down and boots. The brass lamp with an open wick sits between them under the jackfruit tree, the same setting as 10.2 and 10.5. Hands are sound and there is no text. The dark sky at top left and top right is open for both balloons. Both men sit on the ground rather than on a stool or ledge, which is minor.

Nagoji's sleeves are pushed up to the elbows, unlike 11.3 and 11.5 where they reach the wrists. A mottled brand-like patch is painted on the OUTER (top) surface of his left forearm near the elbow, visible at full size. The bible places the brand on the INNER left forearm a hand's width above the wrist, with the white scar beside it, and earlier rows forbid it on the outer forearm. The script does not call for the brand in this beat. Everything else works: Padmini on her sheet (cream Kerala drape, gold border, coiled hair, gold necklace, stick on wet earth, looking down at him), and Nagoji seated with a clean chin, moustache, stud and boots. The lamp, the tree and the lettering space are also fine.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's cream tunic sleeves are pulled DOWN TO HIS WRISTS on both arms, as in panels 11.3 and 11.5. No bare forearms, and no brand, scar, tattoo, blotch, dirt mark or any other marking on either forearm or the backs of his hands. Keep everything else exactly as it was. Padmini stands at left in the cream old-Kerala drape with gold border and no blouse, black hair coiled at the nape, gold necklace and ear studs, and her long wooden walking stick planted on the damp, lamp-reflecting earth; she looks down at Nagoji. Nagoji sits on the low stone ledge under the jackfruit tree at right, looking up at her: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, red sash, talwar at his hip, cream trousers, boots, hands loosely clasped over his knees. The small brass oil lamp with an open wick sits on the ground between them, the horse lines are in the background, and the dark sky and foliage at upper centre stay clear for lettering.

decisions.issues: Clean. In this full-width strip Padmini, with her stick, walks ahead of Nagoji toward a dark thicket at right that looms like an island. They pass raised wooden granaries on stone footings with tiled roofs, under a starry, cloudy night sky. Nagoji is on-model: rust-red turban, clean chin, thick moustache, gold stud, sleeves down, red sash, boots, talwar. Padmini matches her sheet. Hands and gait are sound, and there is no text or anachronism; the gunny sacks are period-plausible. Wide dark sky above and between them takes both of Padmini's balloons.

Minor only: no separate shawl (the indigo pallu drawn over the shoulder stands in for it), and the necklace is the round gold beads from her sheet rather than flat coins, which matches the sheet. The script beat is all there: roots, termite mounds, the crowd of serpent idols under the massive tree, and Revathi lighting the lamp at the largest idol. The night sky at top left is clear for both captions.

Minor: her face is lit warmly from the side and front rather than strongly from below, and the main idol here has three hoods where 12.1 has five. Otherwise on model: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, bead necklace, armlet, bindi and sandalwood line. The dark foliage at top right takes both balloons.

Nagoji is bare-headed, with his long curly hair loose and no turban. Script 12.3 says 'turban and talwar kept', and the chapter 13 bible row puts him in the rust-red turban. Everything else works: Padmini kneeling with palms joined and head bowed before the idols, her walking stick beside her; Nagoji barefoot, with moustache, clean chin, ear stud, cream tunic, red sash and sheathed talwar.
decisions.correction: Nagoji MUST wear his rust-red wrapped turban exactly as on his commander sheet. It covers the crown of his head, with his long curly black hair showing only below it at the sides and nape. He is never bare-headed in this panel. Keep everything else from the previous attempt. Padmini kneels in her cream sari with its narrow gold border, shoulders bare in the old Kerala drape, black hair coiled at the nape, palms joined and head bowed before the stone serpents, her wooden walking stick upright beside her. Nagoji stands a pace behind her, barefoot on the leaf litter, in a cream long-sleeved tunic, red sash and cream trousers, with the sheathed talwar at his hip and his hands folded in front. He has a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold ear stud. The lamp-lit serpent idols, termite mounds and roots sit under the massive tree on the right, and the dark night area at upper centre stays clear of detail for the balloon. No text or letters anywhere.

decisions.issues: Minor: the main idol is single-hooded here where 12.1 shows five hoods; the room, lamp and night lighting are otherwise consistent. The open hand toward the idols reads clearly and the hands are sound. The night sky at top left and top centre takes both balloons.

Clean. A close stone cobra with its hood spread and the lamp flame reflected in its carved eye, lamp at its base, idols and termite mounds behind. The dark sky and foliage at top right takes the two off-panel Padmini balloons. Her tails point to the right edge, toward where the worshippers kneel in front of the idol.

Revathi is seen from behind, so her face is not readable. The sandalwood line is not visible from this angle. Her costume matches the sheet: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, jhumkas, coin necklace and armlets. The lamp is a small bowl, while 13.2 shows a brass lamp on a stand, a minor prop difference. There is clear dark foliage at the top centre and top left for both lines.

Clean. Revathi matches her sheet, with the sandalwood line at the hairline, coin necklace, armlets and jasmine braid. She looks off to the right toward Nagoji, who is out of frame. Her hand clutching the sari is sound. The lamp is a small brass standing lamp, while the neighbouring panels show a bowl lamp, a minor difference. Lettering space is in the dark foliage at the top left and above her head.

Minor. Padmini's palms are pressed together at her forehead instead of showing the fingertips rising from the earth, which is the end point of the same gesture. Her walking stick stands upright, leaning against her forearm. Nagoji matches the bible: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, barefoot, talwar at his hip, curled moustache, clean chin and gold ear stud. Space for Padmini's line is in the dark foliage at the top centre.

Minor. This is a medium shot of Nagoji seated cross-legged rather than a close-up. The lamplight is warm from the right but does not clearly fall on only half his face. The chin and jaw carry stippled skin shading but no beard. The talwar is not visible while he sits. The turban, moustache, ear stud, barefoot feet and clasped hands are all correct. Both captions fit in the dark trees at the top left.

Minor. Revathi's fingers rest at her mouth as her composure slips, so her line will come from behind her hand, which fits the 'unsteady' tag. Nagoji's chin has light stippled shading but no beard, and his talwar is not visible while he sits. Padmini is correctly absent, and Revathi kneels alone by the lamp. Space for the lettering is in the dark canopy at the top centre, between the two figures.

Minor only. Nagoji is barefoot, which matches script 13.3 and the page 13 frames, though the ch13 bible row says boots. This is the only standing panel on the page: 14.2, 14.3 and 14.6 show the pair on the ground, so the page reads as them sinking down after the embrace. Captions fit in the dark sky and foliage at top left (left of the turban) and at top right.

Framed as a medium two-shot rather than the script's close-up, but the beat is clear: Nagoji's mouth at Revathi's jasmine-wrapped hair, both pained, her eyes closed. They sit on the ground, unlike the standing embrace in 14.1, though this matches 14.3 and 14.6. The light texture on Nagoji's jaw is the style's skin shading, not a beard (it also covers his forehead). The ear stud, moustache, rust-red turban and sash are correct, and both hands are sound. Balloons fit over the dark foliage at top left and the upper trunk.

Revathi has pulled back slightly more than arm's length (Nagoji squatting, Revathi kneeling), which fits 14.5's 'stepping close to him again'. She has a tear on her cheek and looks at him, and both are on model. Her necklace is round gold beads, as on her sheet, not the flat coins of 14.2. A faint lamp highlight sits at Nagoji's temple; it is not a forehead mark. The upper-right corner (serpent stones) can take the 14.4 inset without touching her face if the inset stays to the right of about x=0.8. Balloon space: top centre and top left over the dark trunk and foliage, and at left over the stones beside Nagoji.

The script beat is lost. The frame centres on a large lit cobra idol, the serpent stones and the shrine's own oil lamp, which is the brightest point. The distant house with its lamplight is a tiny detail at the top right (about x 0.8-0.87, y 0.2-0.26), and at inset size it would be unreadable or under the Dhanaji balloon. There are also two light sources, not the single point of lamplight the script asks for.
decisions.correction: Compose this small inset as a view looking OUT of the grove, away from the shrine: no serpent idol, no serpent stones, no shrine lamp and no lit foreground anywhere in the frame. Fill the frame with tall black tree-trunk silhouettes in the near and middle distance against a deep blue-black night sky, with a gap between the trunks near the centre. Through that gap, far off and small but clearly the focal point, place a dim tiled-roof Kerala house with ONE single warm point of oil-lamp light at its doorway. That light is the only light in the picture. Keep the dark trunks, the dark foliage and the far house that worked in the upper right of the previous version. Leave a plain dark patch of sky at upper left for the off-panel balloon. No people, no text.

decisions.issues: The over-the-shoulder figure meant to be Nagoji is off model. He is bare-headed with loose curls (no rust-red turban), has a stubbled, bearded jaw (his chin must be clean-shaven) and wears a beige shawl instead of the cream tunic and red sash. He reads as a different man. Revathi is good: dry cheeks, a sad knowing smile, and her sari, coin necklace, jasmine braid and armlet all correct.
decisions.correction: Nagoji is seen from behind over his shoulder in the right foreground and must match his chapter look. He wears the rust-red turban (seen from behind, it covers his crown, with long curly black hair falling from under it to his shoulders), a cream tunic and the broad red sash over his shoulder, and a small gold stud in the visible ear. Any visible sliver of his cheek and jaw is smooth and CLEAN-SHAVEN with no stubble or beard; only the tip of the thick curled moustache may show. No beige shawl, never bare-headed. Keep Revathi exactly as before: dry cheeks, a sad knowing smile, blue-and-gold sari, coin necklace, jasmine braid and gold armlet, with the lamp-lit serpent grove behind her. Keep the dark space above her head for two balloons. Keep both figures low, as in the neighbouring panels: Nagoji seated on the leaf litter, Revathi kneeling close to him.

decisions.issues: The key foreground action belongs to the wrong person. The hand touching the stone serpent's coils is Nagoji's (cream sleeve, reaching right), not Revathi's. Revathi's hand rests on his thigh instead. The rest works: Revathi is close behind him with her face at his ear and eyes lowered, and Nagoji has the turban, moustache, clean chin and ear stud.
decisions.correction: The hand in the foreground touching the stone serpent must be REVATHI'S, not Nagoji's. Show her bare brown forearm with gold bangles reaching into the near foreground, her fingertips lightly brushing the carved coils of a moss-covered stone serpent close to the viewer, large and clearly lit by the small brass lamp. Put the serpent stone on the same side of the strip as Revathi, so her own arm reaches it naturally. Nagoji's hands stay away from the stone, resting on his knee. Beyond the hand, keep the pairing that worked: Revathi kneeling close behind Nagoji, her face at his ear, eyes lowered. Nagoji sits on the ground in the rust-red turban, cream tunic and broad red sash, with a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold ear stud. Keep the blue-black night and the serpent grove, and leave dark open space at upper left above the stones for the whisper balloon. No text.

decisions.issues: Minor only: Padmini has a small pale forehead dot that is not on her sheet. Otherwise it is on model and matches the page 14 grove. Revathi is turned to the serpent idols in her indigo and gold sari with jasmine braid and armlet. Padmini wears the cream gold-bordered sari, carries her stick and leads Nagoji. Nagoji has the rust-red turban, curled moustache, clean chin and gold ear stud. He is barefoot, carries his boots and wears his talwar. The tree trunk at top centre and the dark foliage above Padmini give room for the caption and her balloon.

Third sliver: Revathi has a red vermilion line in her hair parting and a red stroke on her forehead, which mark a married woman, but she is a widow in ch13. Her sari is also drawn over her head, which is off her sheet. The lead rider is a Nagoji double: rust-red turban, red sash and curled moustache, but black jackboots, a chest strap and a dark brown horse that is not Kayal. The cast override deliberately leaves Nagoji out of this panel. Background riders wear rust or pink turbans, against the Madurai troop rule. First sliver: the cellar wall is straight blocks, not curved. Slivers 1 and 2 otherwise work well: ankle bar, rope tearing through bandaged palms with its free end loose, and Keshavrao sinking chained with no rope near him.
decisions.correction: Keep the three diagonal slivers and keep the first two as drawn: the bandaged hands and the iron bar across the chained ankles, and the rope tearing through bandaged palms with its frayed free end whipping loose while young Keshavrao (short hacked hair, faint moustache, grey-brown rags) sinks with his ankles chained in a pair, no rope near him. In the first sliver, make the damp stone wall behind the hands visibly curved, like the inside of a vaulted cellar. In the third sliver, Revathi's face in the smoke is bare-headed, with her sari NOT drawn over her head. Her hair is in its long braid with jasmine and there is a thin pale cream sandalwood line at her hairline. Draw NO red vermilion in her hair parting and NO red mark on her forehead, because she is a widow. Keep her flat-coin necklace, gold bell earrings and the sorrowful smile. Below her, the horses pounding across the wet sand carry Madurai cavalry in white knee-length jama tunics and high-wrapped white or off-white turbans, seen from behind or at a distance. No rider wears a rust-red or red turban or a red sash, and no rider resembles Nagoji. Keep the blue-coated VOC soldiers in black tricornes firing through white smoke, the fort behind them and the plain, unmarked blue flags.

decisions.issues: Minor: Nagoji is in fairly full colour against the desaturated background. The dream treatment still reads, and it is close to the page 7 palette. He is alone, with no clear footprints. The horizon tilts and the fort wall is too tall and too close. The sea is flat and glassy and the palms and sand blow sideways. The open sky at upper right easily holds the caption.

Two background men wear rust-red turbans and red sashes over cream tunics, which is Nagoji's own costume. A third has a red sash. This breaks the bible's Madurai troop look (white or off-white turbans, never red or rust, plain waistbands) and clashes with the white-turbaned riders in 4.1 and 10.5. On a full-width closing panel, readers cannot tell at a glance which man is Nagoji. The script beat of men turning their heads toward the drums is missing: every man is busy with his horse. Nagoji's boots are cropped out of frame. What works: the jackfruit tree and estate house match 10.5. Kayal is on model (bay, black points, quilted ochre pad). Nagoji is buckling on his talwar on model. There are churned hoofprints and the far fort wall has tiny drummer silhouettes.
decisions.correction: Keep the composition that worked: the jackfruit tree with fruit at left, the tiled estate house, the churned and hoofprinted mud, the grey-blue pre-dawn light, and the far fort wall on the right with tiny drummer silhouettes. Keep Kayal in the foreground (bay mare, ochre red-brown coat, black mane, tail and lower legs, quilted ochre saddle pad) beside Nagoji as he buckles on his talwar. Nagoji is the ONLY man in a rust-red turban and a red sash. The other men in the yard are Madurai troopers in knee-length white jama tunics with plain white cloth waistbands, loose trousers and high-wrapped white or off-white turbans (never red, rust or green), plus one or two bare-headed Maravar riders in short dark jackets with white mundus hitched. Show the drums arriving: two or three of these men have paused mid-saddling and turned their heads toward the distant fort wall on the right. Pull the camera back slightly so that Nagoji's brown laced riding boots show on his feet. Keep the open sky above the treeline at upper right low-detail for the captions, and keep the drummers clear of it.
